raw_recipe.headline: Jo's Rosemary Bread
raw_recipe.description: Wonderfully generous with the rosemary, with support from a little black pepper and Italian seasoning, this bread comes out light and fragrant from the bread machine.
raw_recipe.name: Jo's Rosemary Bread

review.reviewBody: If you've ever been to Macaroni Grill, this bread is a duplicate. (Now there's no reason for me to go back...) Fabulous! I made this bread by hand, (1. yeast + 1/4 c. warm water, wait 10 min. 2. Add flour, salt, sugar, oil knead like heck. 3. Add the herbs & pepper [I used oregano insted of an italian blend, and rosemary from my own garden] and knead some more. 4. Let rise an hour or so in an oiled, covered bowl in a warm place. 5. Punch down, let rise another hour. 6. Bake at 375 until browned. 7. Remove from oven, brush with olive oil and sprinkle with coarse salt.)Serve with olive oil and fresh cracked pepper. YUMMY!

Amazing bread! I made this by hand, so I started by proofing the yeast in the water for about 5 minutes, then added one cup of the flour, the sugar, salt, and oil and mixed in my stand mixer on pretty high speed until it was a thick creamy batter (looking almost like pancake batter), 3-4 minutes or so. Then switched attachments to the bread hook and began adding flour gradually, along with the herbs and pepper. Knead just until all dough pulls away from the bowl, then finish kneading by hand (about 5 minutes or so). I make a lot of bread and bread flour is expensive, so I find it easier to buy powdered wheat gluten (which is the main extra is bread flour anyway) and add it according to the package directions (I think it is one tsp. for every cup of flour). Also, if you are lucky enough to live near a Penzy's Spices or ever order from them online, their Tuscan Sunset Seasoning (Italian seasoning) is awesome in this!!! I let this rise is a greased bowl for one hour, then punched down, formed into an oval loaf and let rise another hour. I brushed with olive oil and coarse sea salt before baking, and I also spritzed this with water about 3 times during baking (it gives it that crunchy outer crust, but it still stays soft in the middle). I baked this about 20 minutes at 375 then turned the heat up to 425 for about 10 more minutes. Perfect, delicious bread. My husband has already asked me to make it again soon!

This bread is awesome, just like Macaroni Grille! The only change I made was using milk instead of water because it makes a more tender crust. We dipped it in olive oil and cracked pepper and served it with lasagna. Yummy. It will make your whole house smell great, too! Also makes a wonderful cheesy garlic bread!
I let my bread machine mix and knead and baked it in the oven (375 degrees for 30 min.). It was great! Would be good to dip in olive oil with cracked black pepper like they do in the restaurants.

UPDATE: THIS TASTES EVEN BETTER THAN MACARONI GRILL'S BREAD (I just ate there this past weekend!!!)!!!!! Wow Joe! This is darn good bread!!! I'm not sure if it tastes like Macaroni Grill's bread or not (haven't been to one in ages...), but I bet it does! Made this to go with warm bowls of Andrea's pasta fagioli (also on this site). The combination of the bread and soup was divine! My bf and I really enjoyed our dinner :) I did change things up a bit though.... I put all ingredients in my bread machine (in the order suggested by the manufacturer - wet, dry, yeast on top), turned on the dough cycle and selected the 1.5 lb. loaf setting (this took about 1.5 hours), then took the dough out, punched it down and put it in a greased (with Pam) bowl, turned to coat and covered for 10 minutes. After the dough had rested, I shaped it into a round loaf, covered, and let it rise until doubled in size (a half hour did the trick). Before placing in my 350 degree oven, I brushed the top of the loaf with EVOO and some more (crushed) rosemary and coarse sea salt to taste. The addition of the salt was deelicious and a must IMHO. One thing to note: allow your bread to cool a bit before slicing (we were too hungry to wait, but I wish we had...). Serve with a combination of EVOO, grated Parm cheese and a bit of cracked black pepper, all mixed together for dipping. I think next time I'll add about a tablespoon of Parm to the dough also... Excellent! Thanks for sharing :)

I probably would have given this bread five stars if there wasn't quite so much rosemary. A whole tablespoon gave it an almost medicinal taste. Next time I'll use just two teaspoons and I think it will be great.

I am a regular bread baker and this is quite possibly the best bread recipe I have ever made. I used fresh rosemary and did the whole thing by hand rather than using a bread machine. The bread was delicious. It had a crisp crust and a fluffy interior. Note to beginners that are trying to make their loaves by hand: before placing the dough in the bread pan, roll/stretch bread into a 16 by 8 in rectangle and then tightly roll it up from one of the smaller end. Fold the ends of your roll under ensuring that the ends of the dough will still touch the ends of the pan (so that the dough has something to grip onto as it rises). This procedure will give your bread a nice rounded shape as it rises and give you a wonderful spiraled texture on the inside.

Put it in breadmaker on dough, then cut into 16 pieces, rolled into balls, placed on greased cookie sheet, brushed w/olive oil, sprinkled w/sea salt & crushed rosemary. Baked @ 375 for 17-20 min. Place 9 x 13 pan full of warm water on bottom rack in oven for crusty rolls.

I rate this 4.5 stars. I made it on the dough setting of my bread machine, and finished it off in the oven. I let the dough rest for 10 min., then shaped into an oblong and placed it on parchment paper sprayed with cooking spray. Allowed it to double in size (approx. 45 min.), brushed the crust with a beaten egg diluted with 1 T. water and sprinkled chopped rosemary on top. Baked at 350 degrees until crust was brown and bread had a hollow sound when thumped, approx. 35 min. Placed a shallow pan with hot water in the bottom of the oven to encourage a crusty crust to form on the loaf while baking. I made this bread into grilled cheese sandwiches and paired it with Roasted Tomato Soup, also on this site. A tasty meal on this cool Fall evening.

I used a KA stand mixer. Substituted honey for the sugar, sea salt for regular salt. I heated the water to 105’. Slowly mixed yeast and honey into the water until combined. Let it rest in the mixing bowl for 10 minutes, the yeast mixture will be come frothy. I also sifted my bread flour. Then added remaining ingredients into the yeast mixture. I changed the herbs. I used 2 tablespoons dried onions, 1/2 teaspoon cracked pepper, 1 tablespoon rosemary. I mixed the dough for 4 minutes, then allowed it to rest in the bowl for 15 minutes, turn on flour board knead for about a minute then place in a greased bowl cover with plastic wrap, I let it rise for 1.5 hours. Punch down folded the sides to the middle, then re covered and allowed it to rise an additional hour (technique learned from Julia Child). Then place on a flour surface shaped, placed in a lightly greased loaf pan. I let it rise 1.5 hours. Baked on 375 about 25 minutes. Using a digital thermometer into the middle the temperature should be 190’ . Note I also made dinner rolls using this recipe. I have experimented with different herbs. Each time it turns out perfect. This recipe is a great and now a part of my collection

It was so good, I made another one the next day with these adjustments both times: I used 2 tsp bread machine yeast, and 2 tbs finely chopped fresh rosemary. I added the water salt, sugar and oil first, then the flour, then the yeast. I selected basic white, 1.5 size loaf. I added the rosemary, black pepper, and Italian seasoning when the machine reached the "mix in" stage (it's a Cuisinart bread machine). After the second rise I removed the dough from the machine and kneaded it for about a minute on a lightly floured surface. I placed the dough in a slightly oiled bread pan, covered it with a damp tea towel, placed it in a warmed oven for an hour to rise again. I brushed the top with melted butter after and baked at 375 for 25 minutes. The aroma was awesome and the taste exceptional!

Changes were using 2.25 teaspoons of yeast (instead of 1.5 since an 8oz pack is 2.25 teaspoons), proofing for 35 minutes in a warm oven; after punching down and folding the sides into the center, I shaped into a boule and proofed for another 35 minutes; before putting it in the oven, I brushed the sides with olive oil. I baked at 375F for 20 minutes and then at 425 for 10 minutes (occasionally spritzing with water). Next time I would use milk (instead of water), use 1.5 teaspoons of Italian seasoning (instead of 1/4 teaspoon), and only bake at 425F about 5 minutes (instead of 10).

Was a good recipe. I did not have a bread machine so I followed a reviewers tip on how to make without the bread machine. Mix the lukewarm water and yeast for 10 minutes. Add the flour, salt, sugar, and oil. Knead like heck. Add herbs and pepper. Knead some more. Cover and set in a warm place for an hour. Punch down and recover and set for about an hour. Put in oven at 375 until brown. I used butter on top in lieu of oil. Added coarse salt and voila!!! I dipped in balsamic vinegar and olive oil with cracked peppercorn. Yum.
Nice dough. Baked it in oven on baking stone which gave it a nice crispy crust.
This is a family favorite. Oven: use dough setting. Bake 375° for 30 minutes.

Simple, easy recipe with great results! I followed the directions as is, and this is a family favorite! I leave out the rosemary and Italian seasoning when we want a basic white bread! This recipe is seriously, my favorite ‘go-to’ no-fuss recipe!
Great recipe and my guest loved the bread! Will make it again for Christmas. perhaps will add more rosemary.

I made this exactly as written, and used the 1.5 lb. selection on my bread machine. I used the dark crust selection and it was perfect. The crust was flaky and delicious. I thought the Rosemary was a bit overwhelming, but my daughter disagrees so whatever you think your palate will desire ;)
Perfectly done. Used fresh rosemary. That was the only modification
The first time I made this recipe I was looking for a vegan bread for guests at a party. I loved it so much, it has become my go to bread machine recipe!
